system_prompt_style.evidence_quote: The full evaluation prompt template is included in Appendix D.3.
system_prompt_style.note: Paper-only; prompt mechanism not described in the available text (Appendix D.3 not in evidence).

env_context_strategy.evidence_quote: the agent uses tools to search for relevant papers, open PDFs, and locate and extract target figures or tables.
env_context_strategy.note: The paper describes PDF Extractor RAG as an opt-in retrieval tool that the agent invokes itself.

context_compaction.note: Memory is an append-only chronological store; there is no config surface in the evidence.

observation_format.evidence_quote: For figures, it returns the figure image and caption context. For tables, it returns a structured table representation together with surrounding text when available.
observation_format.note: The 'structured table representation' is mapped to structured_json. The figure images are not screenshots, which is the closest value.

tool_call_format.evidence_quote: the agent first generates a plan outlining its intended actions before producing ex-ecutable code for tool invocation
tool_call_format.note: Sec. 4.1 also says 'we implement this loop using function-calling'. The paper is ambiguous; this is a smolagents CodeAgent-style implementation.

tool_count.evidence_quote: We provide four tools tailored to literature search and paper content access.
tool_count.note: Does not count any built-in final_answer tool from smolagents.

edit_primitive.evidence_quote: We provide four tools tailored to literature search and paper content access.
edit_primitive.note: The tool list, which is the place edit tools would be declared, contains no file-editing tool.

tool_schema_source.note: Appendix D.1 tool specification is not in the evidence.

protocol_standardization.note: No code or dependency list is available.

loop_primitives.evidence_quote: We employ a ReAct-like [35] workflow, in which the agent first generates a plan outlining its intended actions before producing ex-ecutable code for tool invocation.

planning_granularity.evidence_quote: the agent first generates a plan outlining its intended actions
planning_granularity.note: The paper does not describe a stored plan object.

multi_agent_topology.evidence_quote: This section describes the agent implementation used in our experiments.

delegation_mechanism.note: Paper only; there is no agent factory in the evidence.

short_term_state.evidence_quote: Memory is implemented as an episode-level chronological store. We append re-trieved PDFs, extracted figures and tables, and tool observations in the order

long_term_memory.note: Memory is scoped to the episode; cross-run persistence is not discussed.

self_verification.note: The LLM judge is benchmark scoring, not a harness check on the agent's work.

termination_condition.evidence_quote: the agent is constrained by a limited step budget (10 steps by default). If the agent fails to provide a final answer within the allotted steps, it is granted one additional op-portunity to summarize

network_policy.note: The web search tool implies network use, but no policy is described.

tracing.evidence_quote: All tools share a unified interface and return structured outputs that can be appended to memory and traced during evaluation.

eval_hooks.evidence_quote: All turn answers are scored with the LLM-as-a-Judge [12], where GPT-5.2 [17] assigns binary correctness labels under a fixed rubric.
eval_hooks.note: This agent is the reference agent of the benchmark; there is no repo to confirm.

target_domain.evidence_quote: a clean and reproducible interface that couples an LMM with external tools and a persistent memory

model_agnostic.evidence_quote: We evaluate representative four open-source and four closed-source LMMs as agent backbones.

primary_artifact.evidence_quote: We build onsmolagents[21] and adapt it to our episodic paper-centric setting.
